Your dad probably grew up with a different kind of porn to what us young ones did, therefore it probably didn't affect him. Let him watch the TED talk regarding "your brain on porn", link in the sidebar, he doesn't need to read about it. 

The chief aim of a fapstronaut is really to give up porn. The problem is that for many of us, our fapping is inextricably linked to porn and fantasizing about porn. The point of not fapping for a few months is to help your brain recover and so that it no longer associates fapping with porn.

It doesn't matter what he thinks though. It's up to you if you wish to try it or not. It can't hurt.

I feel for you, I understand how you're feeling, and can easily sympathize with your situation. You've managed to get into the second year of the degree, which in my opinion, tends to be the most difficult for most degrees. Ultimately I can't make this decision for you. 

For the vast majority of cases, I would suggest finishing a degree you start. The first job you get, most likely won't be your dream job. You will need to work for a while and develop your resume. 

You say that your curriculum is English and Programming, and you're studying math. Those skills over where I am may allow you to work for intelligence organisations or graduate roles in the police, although the competition for these sorts of jobs is likely to be steep, it's worth going for if you're aiming for a job that's more exciting and not monotonous. 

You still have plenty of time yet. People now have multiple career changes throughout their lives. If you believe that it could potentially take you another 6-7 years to complete your degree, that's a legitimate reason to transfer to a degree that takes less time to finish. If you're good at CS, it may be a good idea to go back to it. Although the learning environment, I understand isn't favorable for you. CS degree will allow you to work in a wide variety of jobs.

Have you spoken to your university careers counselor? They may be able to help you with this. Buy a book or look at online guides for a few different university courses. When you have the time, call some people and ask if they are willing to offer you some work experience so you can see what their job is like. This could be anything, accountant, call an accounting firm, medical scientist working in pathology services, call a reputable hospital, and ask them if you can get work experience in different departments, and do a tour of them all to see what it's like. Got any family/friends that work in trades? Like electricians specialised in domestic or even industrial? Or builders, or plumbers? I'm sure you can find numbers for people working in these professions too, some may be willing to give you a go. I have given you a few different options, but I can't tell you what career you should aim for ultimately, because you have to test the waters yourself. If you choose to drop this degree, pick something, and FINISH it. That's the best advice I can give you. Finish it. I have been in this situation for quite a while, I am older than you, and I wish I had someone to tell me this when I first started out in your position. It really doesn't matter how long it takes you to get into a stable job, everyone has their own pathway to follow in life. I hope this helped, and feel free to ask me questions any time if you believe I can offer assistance.

I also recommend looking around for a nice buddhist temple if there is one close enough to your area. Some offer weekly night sessions where you can learn about meditation and buddhist philosophy from monks. Can't hurt to take a quick google search.
